label: USE CASE 23
title: How AI Helps Doctors Read X-rays

scenes.text: In many hospitals, there aren't enough radiologists to read every scan quickly. [1] Now, AI can look at a chest X-ray in seconds, and flag possible problems. [2] Let's see how AI helps doctors read X-rays.

Here's the flow. [1] The X-ray machine captures the image. [2] A vision model scans it for signs like shadows, spots, or fractures. [3] It highlights suspicious areas with a heatmap. [4] Urgent cases are moved to the top of the doctor's list. [5] And the radiologist reviews, and makes the final call.

[1] The model is trained on hundreds of thousands of X-rays, [2] each labelled by expert radiologists. [3] It learns patterns linked to conditions like pneumonia, tuberculosis, or a collapsed lung. [4] This is image classification and detection, from episode 29.

data.definition: Vision models trained on expert-labelled scans to spot signs of disease and flag them for doctors.

scenes.text: Where does it help most? [1] Triage, so urgent cases get seen first in a busy hospital. [2] Screening, like checking thousands of people for tuberculosis, in areas with few specialists. [3] And a second opinion, catching things a tired human eye might miss.

Here are four terms. [1] Sensitivity, how many real cases the model catches. [2] Specificity, how well it avoids false alarms. [3] Heatmap, the coloured overlay showing where it looked. [4] And regulatory approval, official clearance before a hospital can use it.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think AI will replace radiologists. [2] Today, AI is a tool that helps them work faster, and catch more. Doctors combine the scan with the patient's history, symptoms, and other tests. AI sees only the image.

data.fact: AI helps them work faster and catch more. Doctors combine the scan with history, symptoms and tests.

scenes.text: But there are challenges. [1] A model trained in one hospital may work worse on another hospital's machines. [2] Data must be kept private. [3] And doctors must not blindly trust the AI, a problem called automation bias.
Quick quiz! Who makes the final diagnosis? [1] Pause and think, and if you get it right, comment below! <pause 3.2> [2] The doctor! AI flags and highlights, but the radiologist decides.

scenes.text: Let's recap. [1] A vision model scans the X-ray, and highlights suspicious areas. [2] It's trained on expert-labelled scans. [3] It helps with triage, screening, and second opinions.
